chunks.text: Welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm Emily, and today we're going to a sunny city in Spain, Valencia.
Valencia is full of light, color, and delicious food.
It's a city by the Mediterranean Sea, with beaches, old streets, and friendly people.
Let's explore this Spanish paradise together.
Part two, where is Valencia?
Valencia is on the east coast of Spain.
It is about 350 kilometers south of Barcelona.
The city is next to the sea, and the weather is warm most of the year.
Palm trees, oranges, and sunshine make it feel like summer almost every day.
Part three, a short history of Valencia.
Valencia has a very long history.
It was founded by the Romans more than 2,000 years ago.
Later, it was ruled by the Moors, who brought new culture and architecture.
You can still see this mix of history in the city's buildings.
Roman, Arabic, and Spanish styles together.
Today, Valencia is modern but proud of its past.
Part four, the city and its streets.
Valencia is beautiful and lively.
The old town called El Carmen has narrow streets, colorful walls, and small cafes.
You can walk for hours and see churches, towers, and hidden squares.
The central market is full of fruits, spices, and sounds, perfect for local life.
There are also modern areas with tall buildings and parks full of palm trees.
Part five, the people of Valencia.
People in Valencia are warm, friendly, and proud of their city.
They speak Spanish and Valencian, a local language similar to Catalan.
Family and food are very important in their culture.
People love to meet friends, talk, and enjoy long meals together.
You will often hear laughter and music in the streets.
Part six, food in Valencia.
Food in Valencia is famous all over the world.
The most famous dish is peya, made with rice, saffron, and seafood, or chicken.
It was invented right here in Valencia.
People also enjoy tapas, small plates of food to share, and for dessert, you can try horchata, a cold drink made from tiger nuts, perfect on a hot day.
Part seven, festivals and fun.
Valencia is a city that loves to celebrate.
The most famous festival is Las Fallas in March.
During this week, people build giant sculptures and then burn them at the end.
It's amazing.
There are fireworks, music, and parades everywhere.
It's loud, colorful, and full of joy, a true Spanish fiesta.
Part eight, beaches and the sea.
Valencia is next to the Mediterranean Sea, so there are beautiful beaches nearby.
The most popular one is Malvorosa Beach.
You can swim, play volleyball, or just sit and watch the sunset.
The sea is blue, calm, and warm in summer.
Locals love spending weekends by the water with family and friends.
Part nine, art and architecture.
Valencia is full of art and modern design.
One of the most famous places is the city of arts and sciences, a group of futuristic white buildings.
It includes a science museum, an opera house, and an aquarium.
At night, the lights reflect on the water.
It looks like another world.
Valencia shows how tradition and innovation can live together.
Part 10, nature and green spaces.
In the middle of the city, there's a long green park called Turia Gardens.
It used to be a river, but now it's a beautiful place for walking, cycling, and picnics.
You can see children playing, people jogging, and artists painting.
It's one of the most relaxing places in the city.
Valencia is really a green city.
Part 11, daily life in Valencia.
Life in Valencia is calm and happy.
People start their day with coffee and churros, then go to work or school.
In the afternoon, they have lunch, the biggest meal of the day.
Sometimes they take a short rest called siesta.
In the evening, the streets come alive again with families, laughter, and the smell of paella.
Part 12, goodbye from Valencia.
Thank you for joining me on this trip to Valencia, Spain.
It's a city of sunshine, sea, and smiles.
From its delicious food to its festivals and friendly people, Valencia is full of life.
If you visit Spain, don't forget to stop here and feel the magic yourself.
Goodbye.
Or as people in Spain say adiós y hasta luego.
